 Judgment
Challenging judgment and award dated 30.01.2018 passed by Principal Senior C ivil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-III at Ballari, in MVC .no.790/2014, these appeals are filed.

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts as stated are that in an accident that occurred on 29.01.2013, claimant Shivanna along with his friend Thippeswamy were sitting on stopped motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-16/V-0875 near Rayapura cross, when driver of lorry bearing registration no.KA-18/3428 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle.

In said accident,
claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment at hospital, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.

3. Alleging loss of earning capacity, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
against driver, owner and insurer of lorry.
4. On service of notice, respondents appeared and opposed claim petition on all grounds.
Respondent no.3 - insurer filed objections admitting issuance of insurance policy but, contending that it was subject to terms and conditions which were alleged to be violation.

Even age, occupation,
income as well as disability sustained were disputed.

3
5. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as PW-1 and Dr.K.Lakshminarayana as PW-2 and Exhibits P1 to P8 were marked.
Insurer did not lead oral evidence, but got marked copy of insurance policy as Exhibit R1 with consent.

6. On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver, claimant sustained permanent physical disability as a result and claimant was entitled for compensation from insurer.
It assessed total compensation of Rs.5,65,600/- with 8% interest and held insurer is liable to pay same.
7. Challenging award on quantum, both insurer as well as claimant are in appeal.
8. Sri M.K. Soudagar, learned counsel for insurer at outset submitted that when claimant failed to lead any evidence to establish monthly income, tribunal erred in considering it at Rs.9,000/-.
It was further submitted that though PW-2 was general physician and not orthopedic doctor, his assessment of fracture was excessive and unjustified.
It was submitted that even award under other heads was excessive and unjustified.
It was submitted that even rate of interest @ 8% per annum was excessive and sought reduction.
9. On other hand, Sri Jadai Manjunath, learned counsel for claimant sought enhancement of compensation by dismissing insurer's appeal.
It was submitted that tribunal had awarded inadequate compensation towards pain and suffering and loss of income during laid up period.
10. It was also submitted that though claimant had stated that he was working as agriculturist and earning Rs.16,000/- per month, tribunal erred in taking it at Rs.9,000/- and sought enhancement.
It was further submitted that disability sustained by claimant as assessed by PW2-Dr.K.Lakshminarayana was 25%.
B ut, tribunal considered loss of earning capacity at only 20% and sought enhancement.

11. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
12.

From above submission, occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver, claimant sustaining injuries therein and physical disability therein and liability of insurer to pay compensation to claimant are not in dispute.
Both insurer as well as claimant are seeking for modification of award.

Hence point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether assessment of compensation by tribunal calls for modification as sought for?"
13.

Insofar as monthly income, though claimant stated that he was earning R s.16,000/- per month,
same was not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, tribunal would be justified in assessing it notionally.
But, notional income for year 2013 is Rs.7,000/- as per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Services Committee for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath.

Therefore,
tribunal would not be justified in taking it at Rs.9,000/-.
It has to be considered at Rs.7,000/-.

sentences.text: In order to establish disability, claimant produced wound certificate at Ex.P6 and disability certificate at Ex.P8.
He also examined Dr.K.Lakshminarayana as PW-2.

From said evidence, it is clear that claimant sustained compression fracture of L1, fracture of colles of left wrist and fracture of 5 t h metatarsal of right foot assessed by PW-2 to have caused disability of 25%.

Normally,
fracture of metatarsal does not result in loss of earning capacity.
Though, Ex.P6 is issued by General Hospital at Molakalmuru, Ex.P7 by Dr.K.B.Raghavendra of Challakere, claimant as examined PW-2 - doctor of Ballari, who had not treated claimant.
Despite being a general physician and not a neurologist, he has assessed disability caused due to compression fracture of L1, without giving detailed reasons/basis for his assessment.
Therefore, same would be excessive and unjustified.
Considering age and occupation, it would be appropriate to consider it at 10%.

Thus, future loss of income by applying multiplier would be '17' as follows:
"Rs.7,000/- x 10% x 12 x 17 = Rs.1,42,800/-."
15.
Further, fractures normally take three months to heal.
Since monthly income is re-assessed

,
compensation towards loss of income during laid up period would be Rs.7,000/- X 3 = Rs.21,000/-.
16.
Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Considering three fractures, it would be just and proper to award Rs.40,000/- towards same.
Tribunal has awarded Rs.60,000/- towards loss of amenities, considering nature of fracture and disability sustained

,
award would be excessive.
It would be appropriate to reduce it to Rs.25,000/-.
Tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/- towards medical expenses, even though no medical bills were produced, which would not be justified.
Considering fractures sustained, it is reduced to Rs.5,000/-.
Considering inpatient treatment for 6 days, tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards food, conveyance and other incidental expenses, which appears just and proper.

17. Apart from granting compensation towards loss of amenities, tribunal awarded Rs.88,000/-
towards permanent physical impairment which would not be justified and is set aside.
Lastly, award of interest at 8% without any specific reason would also be unjustified.
In view of decision of this Court in case of Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Smt.Laxmi and Ors., reported 2018 (4) AKR 808, rate of interest cannot be more than 6%.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is reduced to 6%.

18. Thus, claimant is entitled for re-assessed compensation as follows:-
 Sl. Amount  Heads  no. (in Rupees)
 1. Pain and suffering 40,000/-
 2. Loss of amenities 25,000/-
 3. Future loss of income 1,42,800/-
 4. Medical expenses 5,000/-

19. Hence following:
 ORDER  i. MFA.no.101846/2018 filed by  insurer is allowed in part.

ii. Judgment and award dated  30.01.2018, passed by Principal  Senior Civil Judge and Motor  Accident Claims Tribunal-III at  Ballari in MVC.no.790/2014 is  modified.
 iii. Claimant is held entitled for  reassessed compensation of  Rs.2,48,800/- as against Rs.5,65,600/- awarded by tribunal, which shall carry interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iv. MFA.no.103306/2018 filed by claimant is dismissed.
